messages:
Priya Rao: Customer escalated - sporadic 500s and 3000-7000ms tail latency on /v1/chat/completions. They provided two request IDs: req_01aB2c and req_01aB2d. Asking for minimal repro + debug bundle.
Matt Chen: Thanks — can we get the exact curl/SDK payload they used and the full request IDs from logs? Also ask them to run a lightweight curl repro so we can reproduce quickly.
Priya Rao: Pasted what they sent (sanitized): 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "gpt-open-8k",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this long doc..."}],
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
Santiago Vega: OK can you ask for these 3 things: 1) raw request IDs (full), 2) a curl that reproduces, 3) a debug bundle (logs + sdk traces). Provide them a tiny repro template we can drop in.
Claire Nguyen: I'll post small repro snippets for curl + Python/JS/Go they can paste. Keep them minimal and include a header for request-id capture.
Claire Nguyen: Curl snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-8k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"healthcheck"}],"max_tokens":10}' -v
```
Claire Nguyen: Python (requests) quick repro: 
```
import os, requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
data = {"model":"gpt-open-8k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"healthcheck"}],"max_tokens":10}
resp = requests.post(url, json=data, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
# grab request id from X-Request-Id or response body
```
Claire Nguyen: JS (node fetch) tiny repro: 
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-open-8k', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'healthcheck' }], max_tokens: 10 })
  });
  console.log(res.status, await res.text());
})();
```
Claire Nguyen: Go (net/http) tiny repro: 
```
package main
import ("bytes"; "net/http"; "os"; "io/ioutil"; "fmt")
func main(){
  payload := []byte(`{"model":"gpt-open-8k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"healthcheck"}],"max_tokens":10}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions", bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  resp, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, string(b))
}
```
Matt Chen: Also ask them to include response headers (X-Request-Id / x-request-id) or the request-id in JSON body. If they only have partial IDs we'll search, but full IDs speed things up.
Priya Rao: Customer ran curl and got 500 with header x-request-id: req_01aB2c. They attached a tiny log snippet from their side: 
```
2026-03-15T18:22:03Z ERROR api_client.go:142 request failed status=500 request_id=req_01aB2c latency_ms=5123 body="internal server error"
```
Santiago Vega: Good. Tell them how to collect a Redwood debug bundle: run our diagnostic helper (no PII) and attach the resulting tarball. Provide command: 
```
# support helper
curl -sS https://support.redwood.ai/diag.sh | bash -s -- --collect-logs --include-sdk-traces > diag-output.tar.gz
```
Santiago Vega: If they can't run that, ask for: sdk logs (stdout), a verbatim curl command output with -v, and any timestamped trace lines.
Priya Rao: Sent instructions and asked for the debug tarball + exact timestamps around 2026-03-15T18:20:00Z - 18:25:00Z. Also requested the env (region, proxy, HTTP client).
DevX Bot: :robot_face: Note: When you paste snippets, replace keys with $REDWOOD_KEY placeholder. Do not post PII.
Support Oncall: I'll start a quick search for req_01aB2c and adjacent IDs in logs for that time window and post back if I find a server-side correlation.
Matt Chen: If we find a server-side trace, we should check kernel queue, long GC, or backend timeout. Also try forcing model variant gpt-open-4k to see if it's model-specific.
Priya Rao: Customer uploaded diag-output-1753.tar.gz and full request id list: req_01aB2c, req_01aB2d, req_01aB2e. Attachments in ticket.
Support Oncall: Found an internal trace matching req_01aB2c — 503 from model backend, retry later fallback kicked in, then final 500 to client. Sharing server trace snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:22:03Z] route=chat-completions request=req_01aB2c backend=llm-pool-7 status=503 attempt=1 latency_ms=4800
[2026-03-15T18:22:04Z] route=chat-completions request=req_01aB2c fallback=disabled final_status=500
```
Santiago Vega: That looks like transient backend saturation. We'll advise batching / reduce max_tokens and enable automatic retry or fallback to gpt-open-4k as a short-term. Also include guidance to capture sampling of multiple runs (3-5) to confirm reproducibility.
Priya Rao: Sent recommended mitigations and next steps to customer, asked them to test with the minimal repro and the optional model override. Waiting for confirmation. :thumbsup:
